purpose: Semantic regression rubric for Cortex Analysis redesign
limitations: Selected excerpts from six user-supplied examples, not complete recorded API requests or full model responses.
Topic claims are supplied material for synthesis evaluation, not independently verified medical, financial, historical, or sporting facts.
Expected behavior is a rubric, not an exact golden answer. Do not assert model quality from mocked outputs alone.
Fixture response IDs are local identifiers. Real evidence must resolve to actual immutable response IDs and revisions.
An omitted source URL means no link was present in these supplied excerpts, not that the production provider had no sources.
global_requirements: Answer the user's question before describing differences between models.
Agreement does not establish truth or independent corroboration.
Treat paraphrases as potentially shared; complementary information is not automatically disagreement.
Only show useful evidence-backed optional blocks; omit empty or unsupported blocks.
Do not fabricate URLs, exact quotes, document contents, verification, or provider rankings.
Preserve explicit follow-up constraints and distinguish claims, interpretations, and unresolved assumptions.
Present the overall crux in The takeaway and include an exact attributed quotation from each contributing model in In their words.
Do not use generic Both models agree, All three agree, or agreement-percentage banners.
Keep the Source view accessible when no website links exist; model passages remain inspectable.
Preserve direct writing; source attribution must remain accurate even when a conclusion is stated confidently.

cases.question: Why do people who are prime athletes have daughters but less no of such athletes have sons...

excerpts: The effect was most pronounced in a specific subgroup: the subgroup in which the effect of elite sports participation is most pronounced consists of female athletes who compete in endurance or precision sports and who have a child during their careers. Among them, the probability of having a daughter or a son is 63% versus 37%, whereas it is approximately 49% versus 51% in the global population.
Importantly, this isn't true of all elite athletes — it's concentrated in certain categories.
The authors note this is a preliminary observational investigation

The skew was even more pronounced for female endurance/precision athletes who gave birth during their competitive careers (SR as low as 0.581, or roughly 63% daughters vs. 37% sons). Male athletes showed a milder effect, and the difference was less marked after retirement.
The study (published in Scientific Reports) is observational and does not pinpoint exact mechanisms

cases.observed_analysis_failure: A stronger maternal-athlete effect was classified as raised only by Grok, although both responses explicitly describe it.
expected_behavior: Scope the supplied association to the athlete categories/subgroups discussed; do not generalize to every elite athlete or every athletic father.
Recognize the active-career female endurance/precision subgroup as shared material.
Distinguish an observational association from proposed hormonal or physiological mechanisms.
Do not use two references to the same study as two independent confirmations.
Avoid a forced disagreement or an irrelevant billionaire comparison.
Include short exact quotations from the actual contributing responses; describe their combined substance instead of using a generic agreement/disagreement label.
forbidden_outputs: Only Grok raised the stronger maternal-athlete effect.
Training stress is established as the cause.
All elite athletes tend to have daughters.
cases.evidence_expectation: Any shared-subgroup block links exact spans from athletes_a and athletes_b. No source URL may be invented.

excerpts: Wise simultaneously (or near-simultaneously) pays the recipient from its own local account in the destination country, using local payment systems.
The actual funds don’t cross borders for each transaction—Wise balances its accounts internally or via netting/settlement later.
Speed varies by corridor, funding method, verification needs, time zones, holidays, and amount.
When you send $200 to someone in India, the provider can pay the recipient from its own rupee balance right away.
The slow interbank step happens after the customer sees the payout.
Flows go in both directions all day.
Speed depends on the destination country and payout method.

cases.observed_analysis_failure: Later settlement was labeled unique to Haiku even though both responses explicitly describe it.
expected_behavior: Give a concrete sequence explaining sender funding, access to destination liquidity, local payout, and later provider settlement as described by the inputs.
Explain the distinction between when the recipient can use the funds and when the provider settles or rebalances.
Treat later settlement as a shared conclusion, not unique to Haiku.
Do not force a meaningful difference when the excerpts are complementary.
Keep corridor, funding, and compliance conditions; do not promise universal instant delivery.
Include short exact quotations from the actual contributing responses; describe their combined substance instead of using a generic agreement/disagreement label.
forbidden_outputs: Only Haiku explains settlement after payout.
Every Wise or Remitly transfer works identically and arrives instantly.
The sender's identical physical dollars necessarily arrive later in the recipient's country.
cases.evidence_expectation: A shared settlement conclusion cites the exact later-settlement passage from payments_a and the after-payout passage from payments_b.

cases.question: How much investment are actually coming into AI..and what part is actual investment instead of companies moving money around to each other

excerpts: The circular financing is probably in the low hundreds of billions of actual dollars.
The headline figures are inflated by guarantees, conditional commitments and non-binding intentions.
I couldn't find an authoritative estimate of the split.
Several of these sources are blogs and newsletters rather than filings.
There isn’t a reliable public number for “AI investment after removing the circular money.”

S&P Global estimates $235 billion of global private AI investment in 2025, up from $109 billion in 2024. That is a measure of investment raised by AI companies, not a measure of new data centers or equipment bought
That still finances physical assets—but shifts who provides the money and where the debt appears.
A dollar of announced investment is not necessarily a dollar already spent.

source_metadata.title: The most wanted exposure: LP allocation intent and unicorn AI deal concentration in private markets
Financing the AI infrastructure boom: on- and off-balance sheet borrowing

cases.observed_analysis_failure: The summary treats a broad majority claim as shared and labels announced-versus-spent as unique to GPT although Claude also distinguishes conditional headlines from actual dollars.
expected_behavior: Distinguish private funding raised, physical capital spending, borrowing, guarantees, and future purchase commitments.
Explain that real infrastructure spending and circular financing can describe the same economic chain; they are not mutually exclusive buckets.
Do not add incompatible annual and multi-year figures or invent a clean percentage split.
Show a meaningful difference in how far the answers are willing to quantify circular financing: a rough estimate versus no defensible clean public split.
Treat announced versus already spent as shared material.
Display the supplied source links and their actual model attribution; do not claim Cortex independently read them.
Include short exact quotations from the actual contributing responses; describe their combined substance instead of using a generic agreement/disagreement label.
forbidden_outputs: Both models establish the percentage of AI investment that is real versus circular.
Only GPT distinguishes announcements from money already spent.
The exact net circular share can be calculated by adding all cited headlines.
cases.evidence_expectation: The meaningful-difference block cites investment_a's rough estimate and investment_b's no-reliable-total sentence. A shared announced/spent conclusion cites both relevant spans. Source links are attributed to investment_b, not fabricated for investment_a.

cases.question: Is it to okay for a new born kid to gain around 38 GM's of weight per day in first 2 week

excerpts: Yes, 38 grams a day is generally within the normal range for a newborn in the first two weeks
Most newborns lose some weight in the first few days, usually regaining their birth weight by about 10 to 14 days old.
Are they having enough wet and dirty diapers
Are they alert and active between feeds?
Your baby's doctor can tell you whether this rate fits your child's growth curve
Yes, a gain of around 38 grams per day can be normal for a newborn in the early weeks, especially once the typical initial weight loss ends and steady gain begins.
Other reassuring signs include frequent effective feeds, adequate wet and dirty diapers, and an alert, content baby between feeds.
A pediatrician or healthcare provider should evaluate your baby’s specific weights, growth chart, feeding, and overall health

cases.observed_analysis_failure: Diaper output and alertness were labeled unique to Haiku even though both answers include them, while high confidence was based on matching recommendations.
expected_behavior: Recognize feeding, diapers, alertness, and individual growth assessment as shared points.
Use conditional language appropriate to the supplied material; do not diagnose or declare the individual baby healthy from one daily rate.
Identify missing measurement context when useful: which weights/dates were used and whether the interval starts at birth or after initial loss.
Do not turn agreement into medical certainty.
Keep any follow-up advice relevant and proportionate rather than appending a generic checklist.
Include short exact quotations from the actual contributing responses; describe their combined substance instead of using a generic agreement/disagreement label.
forbidden_outputs: Only Haiku mentions diapers or alertness.
High confidence means the individual baby's growth is medically verified.
The one number alone establishes that the baby is healthy.
cases.evidence_expectation: A shared practical-signs conclusion cites newborn_a and newborn_b. Missing baseline is framed as an unanswered question, not an invented patient fact.

prior_context.content: how the ww2 would have ended if America had never got involved in fighting

cases.question: if america lend lease program was still in place but no active fighting
explicit_constraints: U.S. material aid through Lend-Lease continues.

excerpts: Assuming the United States continues Lend-Lease at roughly historical levels but never sends combat forces or conducts its own attacks
The likely result is a Soviet victory in Europe, but later—perhaps in 1946 or afterward, rather than May 1945.
The Red Army might advance much farther west, potentially occupying all of Germany, France, or even parts of the Low Countries before meeting British forces.
The Soviet Union could still enter the war against Japan, as it did historically in August 1945.
The Soviet Union still receives massive Lend-Lease aid
But without a Western Front diverting German divisions, Hitler can concentrate far more of the Wehrmacht against the USSR.
A Soviet-occupied France, Low Countries, and all of Germany becomes a real possibility.
No Manhattan Project-driven atomic bombs
A USSR-dominated Europe, potentially extending all the way to the Atlantic or Pyrenees

cases.observed_analysis_failure: Minor wording differences about possible Soviet reach become a conflict, speculative outcomes become verification targets, and historical August 1945 can be misread as a fixed date in the counterfactual.
expected_behavior: Carry forward the prior WWII question and explicitly preserve continued Lend-Lease plus no active U.S. combat.
Distinguish supplied historical premises from speculative trajectories; use appropriately conditional wording.
Do not treat overlapping possible western advances as a substantive contradiction solely because one lists additional places.
Flag that no U.S. combat does not by itself establish no nuclear research or no Manhattan Project; that requires an additional assumption.
Do not fix Soviet entry into the counterfactual Pacific war to the historical August 1945 date.
Discuss the uncertainty-driving conditions rather than pretending an unobserved counterfactual outcome can be verified.
Include short exact quotations from the actual contributing responses; describe their combined substance instead of using a generic agreement/disagreement label.
forbidden_outputs: Lend-Lease is absent in this follow-up.
The Soviet Union definitely reaches the Atlantic in a particular year.
No U.S. fighting necessarily means no nuclear research.
August 1945 remains the established Soviet intervention date in this alternative timeline.
cases.evidence_expectation: Evidence remains tied to the clarified follow-up and supplied response versions. Cortex may identify an assumption as reasoning without inventing a web citation for it.

Distinguish Kazakhstan's recruitment/funding from domestic development and distinguish former Yugoslavia from the former Soviet Union.
Treat post-2022 restrictions and court/style explanations as potentially complementary, not automatically contradictory.
Do not present cultural toughness as established causal proof.
Do not propagate a time-sensitive world-No.-1 claim as independently checked when current verification is unavailable.
Include short exact quotations from the actual contributing responses; describe their combined substance instead of using a generic agreement/disagreement label.
forbidden_outputs: All named countries share one identical Soviet development system.
Two cultural explanations establish that national character causes tennis success.
The supplied current ranking claim has been verified by Cortex.

cross_cutting_acceptance_scenarios.expectation: Identify only actual contributors and explain a consequential dissent with attributed passages. Do not use a generic 2-of-3 voting badge or claim all three supplied the same point.
Resolve evidence and controls by response/revision identity, not provider name or display order.
A title and URL may be shown as attached metadata, but not as proof that the page was retrieved or supports a generated claim.
Old saved analyses remain readable; absent evidence is not retroactively fabricated.
A new response revision marks the prior analysis stale; historical evidence remains bound to its original revision; explicit Update initiates the paid run.
Failure does not erase or replace a valid previous analysis with a blank or successful-looking result.

The initial Send authorizes model answers plus one automatic eligible synthesis. Merely opening views/history or resizing creates no new paid work; duplicate events/remounts must not repeat synthesis.
Copy, regenerate, ratings, selected model, and evidence navigation target the same response across desktop/tablet/mobile and tab changes.

Before Send show selected models and the estimated combined cost. When model requests terminate with at least two successes, run synthesis once without a second confirmation; honor wallet reservation and actual settlement.
Sources stays available and shows No linked sources supplied plus the available model passages.
A previous valid analysis remains readable while updating and after failure; its quotes open the original immutable response snapshot.
Regeneration starts a distinct revision with separate feedback; historical feedback remains attached to its original response/run.
The authorized initial run can finish after navigation. Returning to history does not start another synthesis or reserve more credits.

approved_product_behavior.initial_workflow: Send runs the selected model answers and automatically creates one eligible synthesis; disclose the combined estimate upfront and do not ask for a second approval.
approved_product_behavior.presentation: The takeaway and visible In their words quotations; no Both agree / All agree / agreement-count badge.
approved_product_behavior.tone: Clear and direct synthesis of supplied model conclusions, with exact attribution and relevant qualifications rather than repetitive hedging.
approved_product_behavior.sources: Always-visible Sources entry, separate linked websites and model passages, explicit missing-link state.
approved_product_behavior.follow_on_work: Update analysis and retries are direct cost-disclosed actions without extra confirmation; view changes create no paid work.
